chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man said to me, 'What did you say when you entered upon Abu Ja'far at Al-Rabza?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I said: O Allah, You suffice from everything and nothing suffices from You, so suffice me with whatever You will, and however You will, and from wherever You will, and whenever You will.'

key_terms.الربذة: Al-Rabza, a location where the Caliph al-Mansur resided or was held.
key_terms.فَاكْفِنِي: So make me sufficient/suffice me (imperative to Allah).

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for entering the presence of authority or in times of distress according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the strategic use of du'a during the tense period of the Abbasid Caliphate, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) sought divine protection from the Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur in Al-Rabza. The supplication emphasizes Tawakkul by asking Allah to suffice the believer in whatever manner, place, or time He wills, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on divine omnipotence over political power. It serves as a model for seeking 'kifayah' (sufficiency) in times of distress and fear of authority.
